lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Oof, I'm finally here! At least the 6 hours went by fast on Delta One! ;)

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TATA! You're BACK!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We waited for you for a hundred years.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A hundred MILLION years!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, up! Up up up!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm the tallest! Giddyup, Tata!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello, Rose. Please keep your arms and legs inside the uncle at all times.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, LOOK. A sparkling diamond gold dumpling squishy!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's limited edition. There are only two in the whole world. You can squeeze it!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's the shiniest dumpling I've ever seen. And I've seen a LOT of dumplings.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Come on, Tata! Let's go!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! Deedee made rhubarb crisp for you. It's cooling RIGHT NOW.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I already licked the spoon. Don't tell.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we had better hurry. Before somebody licks the rest.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There's my Tommy!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And my girls! Come here, come here.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom, you're skin and bones. Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Where are my reading glasses? I had them one second ago. I need to read the timer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Deedee. They're on your head.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: So they are. Not one word to Boppy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I brought you a sourdough loaf. Baked it yesterday. It flew here on my lap.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Your bread and my rhubarb crisp. Now THAT is a meal.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: A sliver for me. Just a sliver. Sourdough gives me gas.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom, EVERYTHING gives you gas.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And I eat it anyway. That's love, Tommy.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom! Good. I'm not feeling good. It's the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee! A mud blob is taking your PIE!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That was UNCALLED for!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That's my GOOD tin! Grab your shoes. I'm coming with you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I TOLD you something lives in that pond. Twenty years I've been saying it. Nobody listens to Boppy.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'd come, but the stomach. Bring me back that fish.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Crumbs! Rhubarb crumbs. That little thief went right through here.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. The mud is MOVING.

lines.speaker: Mudling
lines.text: Blub. The pie went that way. You can't have it. Blub.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Okay, everybody. Tata is in front. I'm in charge of choreography. FIGHT!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Good job, girls. The crumbs keep going north.

lines.speaker: Skeeter Swarm
lines.text: Bzzz. Somebody smells like rhubarb. Bzzzzz.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Ew. Ew ew ew. Nobody touch my hair.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Everybody okay? Itchy isn't hurt. Keep walking.

lines.speaker: Pond Grump
lines.text: Grrrumble. You're standing in my puddle. And the small one is LAUGHING at me.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm not laughing. I'm giggling. It's different.

lines.speaker: Pond Grump
lines.text: That's IT. Soggy Slap. For the giggler.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There. Good as new. Try not to do that again.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Hugs for everyone. There. All better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The crumbs go around the pond. Toward Boppy’s fishing spot.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy says the Big One lives over there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Boppy also says the stomach thing is serious. Stay close.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: THERE! The thief! He still has the tin!

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: GLUB. Is that a pie? For me?

lines.speaker: Big Mudling
lines.text: Blub. For you, boss.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: It fits. I'm a king now. GLUB.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That's my GOOD tin, you overgrown handbag!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, he looks like a turtle wearing a hat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody touches Deedee’s crisp. Everybody ready?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee kisses it better.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tommy, you stand in front of whoever it stares at. Rosie, make it laugh. Then we try again.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Glub. Nobody ever made me laugh before. You can have your tin back.

lines.speaker: The Big One
lines.text: Glub. Fine. Take your tin. I'm going back in the pond to think about things.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: My tin! And look. Half the crisp is still in it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The Big One ate the other half. I saw crumbs on its chin.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Then we split this half. Everybody home. Boppy has to hear about this.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You found the Big One? I TOLD everybody. Twenty years.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It had this stuck in its lip.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My LURE! I lost that in 2006. Still shiny. Unlike me.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Keep it, Tom. For luck. The fish clearly didn't want it.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Sit. Everybody sit. Half a crisp is still a crisp.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: This is the best half a crisp I ever had.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you're staying the WHOLE week, right?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The whole week. And nobody is stealing anything else.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Slow down. Everybody eats too fast. My stomach.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft. He's never home.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...He said he'd be home.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Well, well, well...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look who flew three thousand miles to see me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I flew three thousand miles to see you. The starter is the bonus.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Main event. I'll take it. Sounds premium. Like your seat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My call time got pushed to Thursday. The lead actor lost a shoe. I already found it. So I'm all yours.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Also, something is up. The sky over Griffith Park went purple this morning. Not sunset purple. Weird purple.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: All yours. I like that. We'll look, together. One quick stop first. My starter has been alone for a week.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Olivia dropped her off this morning. Family trip to the desert. No dogs at the hotel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's been sitting on your porch since eight. I tried to take her to the loft. She refused.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Also, your starter was bubbling out of the jar, so I baked a boule with it. Don't be mad.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mad? I'm proud. And a little mad.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Tom tears off the heel and holds it up. "Sit." Nara sits, wiggling all over. "Paw." She gives him her paw. Very, very hard.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: She gets the bread. Tom gets a lick.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. Very polite. Very strong paw.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello, Bready Mercury. Did you miss me? You missed me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. Look at those bubbles. Proud of you.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You talk to that jar more than you talk to me.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The jar gets fifty grams of flour. You get the whole week.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...And you steamed my shirts for the flight. You win. You always win.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I'll take it.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara is at the front window, whining. Her tail is down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Look outside. Is the street... purple?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mr. Washington! Is everything okay?

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Tom. Back in 1979, this whole block...

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He's been on "this whole block" for a while, babe.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Such a nice afternoon. It should always be this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me, smog. That was UNCALLED for.

lines.speaker: Smoglet
lines.text: Cough. Nice street. We're going to sit on it for a while. Forever, actually.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Remember movie night? You threw the whole popcorn bowl.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was startled. Briefly. With dignity.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It was a battle plan. You just didn't know it yet.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Everybody breathe. Through the nose. Not the smog.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: They're gone, but he's still out of it. Look at him.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Nobody needs to go anywhere. Nobody needs to get any older.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's not a Mr. Washington sentence. Let's check on the boulevard. Miss Odette and Doña Carmen.

lines.speaker: Miss Odette
lines.text: Stirring. Stirring. The gumbo never has to be done, baby. Isn’t that nice?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She's made that gumbo every day for fifty years. It's never once been "never done."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The smog wants everything to stay exactly the same. Forever. That's not a nice afternoon. That's a hostage situation.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: The pupusas are fine. Everything is fine. It's always this afternoon. Why did I ever flip them?

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sniffs the comal. She sneezes. The smoke smells like the hills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Nara is right. That's not kitchen smoke. That's the same purple stuff.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe. Look north. It's all coming down off the hills.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The Observatory. The pipes on the side are pumping it out like a smoke machine on a bad set.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then that's where we're going. Nara, stay close.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara presses against Tom’s leg. She's not letting him go anywhere without her.

lines.speaker: Ticket Flurry
lines.text: Street cleaning. Tuesday. Eight to ten. You didn't read the sign. And the smog says we can stay forever.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I take the Metro. You have nothing on me.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up, everybody. Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Contested. Appeal granted. Keep going.

lines.speaker: Canyon Coyote
lines.text: Nice hike. You look like you have snacks. And the dog looks like a snack.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara’s hackles go up. She stands right in front of Tom.

lines.speaker: Canyon Coyote
lines.text: Pack Howl. For the fluffy one.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up, everybody. Wardrobe says nobody is cut from this scene.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Quick wardrobe adjustment, quick heal, and a quick kiss for the road. Ready, babe?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Ready. Kiss accepted. The Observatory is up at the top left. Follow the purple.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The ground is humming. That's never a good sign. I've seen this movie forty-seven times.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: RUMBLE. Somebody plugged my pipes. Now everything is stuck. I LIKE stuck.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Stuck means nothing moves. Nothing changes. Nothing ever has to say goodbye.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody says goodbye. Then they come back. That's what planes are for.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Things have to move.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara barks at the hill. Once. Very loudly. Then she checks that Tom saw.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Well, well, well... looks like we're in a bit of a shaky situation.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Cut. Reset. Back to one, everybody.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Babe, heal right after the Aftershock. When it clogs up, hit it with water or sparkle. Or one of our Tombos.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Rumble. You asked how I was doing. Nobody has asked in a million years.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: ...I'll let things move. A little. Two inches a year. That's my best offer.

lines.speaker: The Big Shake
lines.text: Rumble. Fine. The pipes are clear. I'm going back under the hill to think about my choices.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Look. The sky is blue again. LA blue. Slightly brown, but blue.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somebody plugged those pipes on purpose. Smog doesn't do that by itself.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Spooky. I love it. I hate it. Let's go check on Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: ...smelled like gumbo on a Saturday night. Zydeco from the boulevard. Kids on every porch.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Where was I? Oh. I was done. That was the whole story.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Funny. For a while there I didn't want anything to change. Then I remembered the best parts all came from things changing.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Keep the old windows, though.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: Keep the old windows. Smart man.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Doña Carmen says the pupusas came out perfectly crispy. Miss Odette is sending over gumbo. The whole block is cooking.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara leans on both of them at once. Tiny excited puddle. Nobody minds.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Home. Both of them. Okay. Good.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! Boppy has been waiting by his window since BREAKFAST. He has his fishing hat on.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. He's never caught a fish.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we had better go help him not catch one.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: There's my Tommy!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Back already! Look at you. Did they feed you out there? Never mind. I'll feed you.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. Good. Sit down. No. Don't sit down. We're going fishing.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The Whisker Perch. Whiskers like a cat. I saw it at Cattail Pier in 1994. Nobody believes me.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nobody believes him.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, is the Whisker Perch real?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Real as my heartburn, kiddo.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm bringing a notebook. For science. And for proof.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And I'm bringing THIS. My pepper jar. Homegrown, pickled in 1989. Older than your mother.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Not one pepper for me either. Peppers give me gas.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Deedee. EVERYTHING gives you gas.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Who told you that.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. At the crisp.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tata is on thin ice.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I have three pies in, so I'm staying put. Do NOT let him eat peppers on an empty stomach.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I never eat peppers on an empty stomach. I eat them on a full stomach. Then it's empty.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: Boppy! The usual? Ginger, peppermint, and a little honey for the stomach.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The stomach thanks you. The stomach is still complaining. But it thanks you.

lines.speaker: The kettle
lines.text: The kettle whistles, low and long. Oolong leans in to listen.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: The kettle says a man in a long coat has been buying up gold coins at Penny’s. Paying double. Never takes his hat off.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: On Long Island? Nobody here pays double for anything.

lines.speaker: Oolong
lines.text: The kettle also says it'll rain on Tuesday. The kettle is wrong a lot. Enjoy the pier.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Did I ever tell you about 1970? Sit down. This takes a while.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You did. Forty times.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then forty-one. First year of college. Cross country. Five miles through the woods, up the big hill, and I never breathed hard.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Last hill, I passed the whole field. Champion. They put my name on a plaque. The plaque is in a box. Somewhere.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can you still run that fast?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Sure. Sure I can. I just choose not to. It's bad for the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Race you to the pier, Boppy!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Last one there's a soggy sock!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Why is everybody walking like they're going to a fire? Slow down! My stomach is doing flips!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Boppy speed, everybody. We walk at Boppy speed.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: This is the spot. Forty years, this spot. Now everybody be QUIET.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I AM BEING QUIET.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose. Inside voice. Outside.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Shhh. Quiet on the pier, everybody. Boppy has a whole system.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom holds the tackle box. I cast. The fish comes. Nobody talks. That's the system.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...Any minute now.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's been a minute. I wrote it down.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Snack. A pickled pepper settles the stomach.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee said NO peppers.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Deedee isn't here.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: BLORP.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA! A FISH! A HUGE ONE! WITH A MUSTACHE!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's no perch. That's OLD IRON-GILL. I saw him in 1994! I TOLD everybody!

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. Something smells like peppers.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: MY JAR!

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: GULP. Spicy. I love it. Bye.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That was UNCALLED for!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Pickled in 1989. Nobody takes Boppy’s peppers. NOBODY.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He went west. Into the Whispering Marsh. Come on. And nobody walk fast.

lines.speaker: Soggy Sock
lines.text: Squelch. Have you seen my other sock? It looks just like me. It's ALSO angry.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, that sock has a FACE.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Marsh junk. Everything people drop out here ends up grumpy about it. Like me, at the DMV.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. Again.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Socks. Out here. Nobody keeps track of their socks anymore.

lines.speaker: Tangle
lines.text: Snarl. Somebody cast me badly in 1997. I've been in a knot ever since. Nobody gets past ME.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Excuse me? Nobody gets past ME. That's MY line. I was saying that at Rikers before you were a knot.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. Again.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy, you're breathing kind of hard.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'm breathing EXACTLY as hard as I want to.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We take it slow. Iron-Gill’s wake goes northwest, toward those big reeds.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The old reeds. When I was a kid we said there was a sundial back in there that told the wrong time.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Sundials can't tell the wrong time. That's not how sundials work.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's what I said.

lines.speaker: Old reeds
lines.text: Iron-Gill’s wake goes straight into the reeds. There used to be a boardwalk through here. Something big and soggy is sitting in front of it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we ask it nicely to move. Iron-Gill isn't keeping that jar.

lines.speaker: Snag
lines.text: Creak. This was a boardwalk once. Now it's MY spot. Everything catches on me here. I like it.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You're sitting on the way to Sundial Hollow. Shove over.

lines.speaker: Snag
lines.text: Make me. Slowly. I'm very heavy when wet. I'm always wet.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, it's a LOG with a BOOT.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good. Nobody is missing. Again.

lines.speaker: Old reeds
lines.text: The Snag rolls over, creaks, and drifts off into the shallows. Behind it, the old reeds lean apart around a narrow, mossy boardwalk.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A secret boardwalk. Of course there's a secret boardwalk.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Not secret. Just old. Like me. Nobody comes back here anymore.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine. It hasn't changed. It still says seven.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's the AFTERNOON. The sun is right there. Sundials can't be wrong. That's not how sundials work.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That's what I said.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata! Something shiny is stuck in it!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A coin. Wedged right under the pointer. Somebody pushed this in on purpose.

lines.speaker: The sundial
lines.text: Click. The shadow swings all the way around the dial and settles on the right hour.

lines.speaker: The spillway
lines.text: Up north, the spillway gurgles, then glugs, then drains away to mud. The way to the Deep Pool is open.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It MOVED. Shadows don't move like that. I'm writing this down. In pen.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Old gold. Keep that in your pocket, Tom. Penny will want to hear about it. Penny wants to hear about everything.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Now. The Deep Pool. That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The Deep Pool. Nobody has ever seen the bottom. My father said it goes all the way to Ohio.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. The old man. And his small, loud friends.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: You took my jar.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: I took your jar. Forty years you sit on that pier and you never once come to visit. You only ever bring HOOKS.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, he's sad! And spicy!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He's a FISH, kiddo.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Tom. Tackle box. We do this the old way.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Quiet on the pier, everybody.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Headcount. One, two, three, four. Good.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He belches every third turn, Tom. Heal right after. When he dives, hit the water hard, or do our Tombo.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. Fine. FINE. Take your jar. It was too spicy anyway.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My jar. Still sealed. Still hot.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And look at that. Forty years, and I finally caught Old Iron-Gill.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Technically he caught your jar, and then we caught him. I'm writing it down anyway. For proof.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Put the date. Put the time. Use the sundial. It works now.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Go on, you old bucket. Catch and release. I'll come by. No hooks.

lines.speaker: Deep Pool
lines.text: Iron-Gill sinks back into the Deep Pool, burping softly. The bubbles look almost friendly.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Boppy, can we go home now? I want to tell Deedee EVERYTHING.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Everything except the pepper part.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: ESPECIALLY the pepper part.

lines.text: She does three laps around Tom, slams into his shins, and leans on him with all forty pounds.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hi. Hi. Yes. I know. I was gone FOREVER. It was six days.

lines.speaker: TNB

lines.speaker: Toni

lines.text: (on the radio) ...kkkt... Stage 7! The big door just unlocked itself! From the INSIDE! Is that bad? That feels bad.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. A school. At NIGHT. With MONSTERS, probably.

lines.speaker: Tom

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Every clock in this hall says a different time.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That one says four. That one says nine. That one is going BACKWARDS. I teach time, Tom. This is personal.

lines.text: Tata! Tata! SPARKLY FOOTPRINTS!

lines.speaker: Amy

lines.text: Oh, I remember you. Fourth grade. You and me. Every Friday.

lines.speaker: Amy

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up! Everybody up! Walk it off. Hydrate. We go again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You know I was terrified of that thing? Every Friday. That's why I threw so hard.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. You threw one at me at Thanksgiving. I was holding a pie.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You caught the pie, though.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I caught the pie.

lines.text: BRRRRRING. One bell. Right on time. Then silence. The good kind.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: (on the intercom) ...ksssh... Attention, please. The Cafetorium doors are OPEN. Parents, please wait in the hall. There's something in the Cafetorium.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori’s brother, please go into the Cafetorium. Thank you. ...ksssh.

lines.text: The footprints go in there. The sign-up sheet is in there.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the something.

lines.text: It's covered in RED.

lines.text: Click. Wrong. Wrong. Wrong. Every name on this sheet is written wrong.

lines.text: Kowalski has a W. Delgado has a G. Gregori has TWO Rs, and nobody ever writes them neatly.

lines.text: That's the conference sign-up sheet. Thirty parents are waiting for it.

lines.text: A hundred thousand wrong answers, I've marked. Every quiz. Every spelling test. Every crooked line.

lines.text: Nobody ever grades ME. Nobody ever writes NEAT next to ME. So tonight, I grade the grown-ups.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You took the sign-up sheet to grade it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: And the bells. And the clocks. Late is late. Points off.

lines.speaker: Rose

lines.speaker: Amy

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everybody. Walk it off.

lines.text: The Red Pen clicks itself shut, rolls off the podium, and hops away down the hall toward the second grade room.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: ...It's going to my desk. Of course it's going to my desk.

lines.text: For two hours, Amy talks to thirty parents. Grace hands out cookies. Rose tells everybody the pen had glasses. Tom stacks chairs and nods calmly.

lines.speaker: Principal Pruitt
lines.text: Mrs. Gregori. Best conference night in thirty-one years. Not one parent cried. Well. Mr. Delgado. Happy tears.

lines.text: This is for you. My Golden Stopwatch. Thirty-one Field Days. It's never once stopped early.

lines.speaker: Amy

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Oh. A text. From Justin.

lines.speaker: Amy

lines.text: Girls. Did we save a cookie for Dad?

lines.text: Tata. Tata. There's a man.

lines.text: I'm keeping a list too. Mine has a chart.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: If somebody gets called and can’t move, I’ll walk them on. And if we need a friend in a hurry, wave to the bench.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? It calls one of us every turn. Move before it goes again, or Tom will walk you on.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: ...ON TIME. ON TIME. ON TIME.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: It’s fine. They’re all on time. I am not.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Nobody is cancelling you. You just never got a boarding pass. Here. Take mine.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Something is dropping out of the gate clock. A gold coin, with a little clock face. Number nine.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s warm. Whatever Vance was holding, it wasn’t his.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Attention, passengers. The departures board has been updated.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. LONG ISLAND: CLOSED. LOS ANGELES: NOW BOARDING.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. The little green town. It’s turning orange. No. Amber. Like a caution light.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is Deedee okay?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’m calling her. I’m calling her right now.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s ringing. It’s just ringing. Mom always picks up. Mom picks up on the FIRST ring. She picks up before it rings.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sit down. Everybody. Deep breath.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad’s in his recliner. Mom has the crisp. They’re fine. They’re probably fine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey. We’ll go get them. Whatever he did, we’ll fix it. Things come apart. I fix things.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll go get them. We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Which one is Los Angeles?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The orange one. It’s the only one still open.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: And it’s where Nara and TNB live. It’s home. Our other home.

lines.speaker: Speaker
lines.text: DING. Attention, passengers. Los Angeles is now boarding. All other gates remain closed.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The gold clock on the big door finally has hands. They’re pointing at 3, 4, 6, 8.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s my address. The door knows where I live.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The door knows where you live? That’s so creepy. I love it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Home. Okay. Good. I have a very good couch and a very bad idea of what’s in the fridge.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara hears the word home. Nara is already pressed against the door, vibrating.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody together. Nobody gets left behind in the layover. That’s the only rule.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That’s two rules. Together, and nobody gets left.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: They’re the same rule, Grace.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dog on a leash. Girls on the buddy system. Here we go.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Jefferson Park. Same jacarandas, same lemon tree, same wood door.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nothing is paused here. The sprinklers are even on.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It smells like lemons. And a little bit like a burrito.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the lemon tree and Doña Carmen’s. Welcome to 3468.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, you live in a real grown-up house. With flax.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: What’s flax?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The red grass by the steps. It looks like it’s waving.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s waving at ME.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Wood door. A welcome mat in Japanese. Not one thing out of place.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve known you thirty-some years, and I pictured a pile of laundry and a gaming chair.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB is the reason nothing is out of place.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m the reason there are coasters.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara checks the front gate. A squirrel is on the fence. Nara loses her entire mind.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Come in. I’ll show you where I live. Mind the dog. And the sourdough.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. TATA. There’s a jar. It’s bubbling. It’s ALIVE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s Bready Mercury. He’s nine years old, he’s flown Delta One, and he’s the only one in this house who gets fed on time.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You named your bread Mercury? Like the planet?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Like the singer. He’s a showman. He rises on command.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can he do a trick?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He rises. Every day. Without being asked. It’s the best trick anybody in this house does.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I do a trick where I turn a lump into a bowl.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You do. Yours is better. Don’t tell Bready.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. There’s a picture of us. On the wall. In the nice frame.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s one of me with a sandwich. It’s my best side.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s the wall I walk past every morning. Before work. Before coffee.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I say good morning to the two of you.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Every morning?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every morning. Rose usually says it back. In my head.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I said it back just now. Good morning, Tata.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Good morning, Rose.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So this is your house.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s yours too. I mean it. A snow globe called Long Island, and a house called this one. Both. Always both.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. That wall is the nicest thing I’ve seen in a house in years.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s an Ikea frame. Don’t make it weird.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a very nice Ikea frame.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara has climbed onto the couch. This is not allowed. She looks right at Tom. It is allowed.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. Next stop, the loft. Everybody’s coming. I’ll show you where I break things on purpose.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: This is it. The loft. Kiln, wheel, and a lot of clay in places clay shouldn’t be.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s so many mugs.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Can I touch the clay?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Rose. Come here. Wet hands. Sit. Put your thumb in the middle. Don’t push. Just open it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s a hole.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s a bowl. It just doesn’t know yet.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Mine is leaning.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Leaning is a style. It’s called Pisa.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He taught my six-year-old to center clay in four minutes. I’ve been trying to get her to center her cereal for two years.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Clay doesn’t move. Cereal moves.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: So. Tom. Tell me one thing he does when he thinks nobody is watching.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He checks the front door three times before bed. Tells me it’s for the dog.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He did that at nine. He told Mom it was for the cat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You had a cat?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: We never had a cat.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The first night I fired the big kiln alone, it was three in the morning. I looked up and he was standing in the doorway. With a thermos and a blanket. Just in case.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That is exactly him. He’s been standing in doorways with a thermos since he was nine.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He thinks I didn’t see him. I fired a second kiln so he’d have a reason to stay.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. I like you. Don’t tell him.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He’s standing right behind you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was looking at a mug.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s a very nice mug.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Look! I made a bowl! It has a hat! The hat is a lump!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s the best bowl in the loft. It goes in the kiln tonight. You can pick it up when we’re all home safe.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Love the block. Love the lemons. So many lemons. What is that, a jacaranda? Needs less.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me. Who are you?

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I fix places. This place has a lot going on. Too much color, too many porches, a dog doing something on a lawn.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara, offended, does it again. On purpose.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s a neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: That’s the problem with a neighborhood. Notes.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: He lifts a clipboard. The top page says NOTES: LESS. He snaps his fingers.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He took the pink off the jacaranda!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can’t just take the pink!

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I can take the pink, the yellow, and the music out of that window. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe. Quiet sells.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I have twelve kids in my room who’ve had harder mornings than you. You don’t scare me. Colors back, please.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I don’t put things back. I take notes. Anyway, Mr. Prime will handle the intersection. Do take a look at the traffic. It’s very stationary.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: He walks off into the grey, humming a jingle that never resolves.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He’s turning the whole block into a backlot. And he stopped something. Look at Mr. Washington.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s amber. It’s warmth that got stuck. Doña Carmen’s is right there, and the Alvarez house is down 2nd.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We check on the neighbors first.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Doña Carmen turned into candy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: She’s amber. Mid-sentence.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: She’s still pointing at the volcano.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Amber is just warmth that got stuck. You don’t break it. You give it somewhere to go.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Warmth. We’re good at warmth. Everybody find the warmest thing in the room.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The comal! The pupusas!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Tom lifts a pupusa off the comal. It’s still hot. Steam is coming off it, in a room where nothing else is moving.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Doña Carmen. It’s Tom. Nobody on this block has ever left your door hungry. We’re here to eat. Please wake up.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sits at Carmen’s feet, tail wagging in a perfect circle, and sneezes on the amber.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: A crack runs up the amber like sugar glass. Then another. Then it falls away in warm gold flakes.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: ...and THEN I told the man, the loroco is not optional. Tom! When did you get here? Why is everything so quiet?

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Where did my pupusas go?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You were amber for a little while.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: I was what? I had a whole sentence. I lost the sentence. It was a good sentence.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A man in a grey suit did it. His name is Marlowe.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: That man stood on my step and said my sign was “too busy.” I said the sign is busy because the food is good.

lines.speaker: Doña Carmen
lines.text: Go next door. The Alvarez house. They didn’t get any pupusas today. Take these. Feed the children first. The grown-ups will pretend they’re not hungry.

lines.speaker: Daisy
lines.text: Tom! Tom! Everybody stopped! Abuela stopped in the middle of saying NO!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. They’re amber. The grey got in through the front door.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Heat is just movement. When the girls can’t sleep, we run. Nobody stays stuck when they’re moving.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You mean...

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody up. Girls, with me. We’re running laps around the kitchen table.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Run with us, Mommy!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap one! Knees up, Rose!

lines.speaker: Don Beto
lines.text: ...and that is a FOUL! That is a foul! Who has the remote?

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap two! Grace, don’t look at the camera!

lines.speaker: Tony
lines.text: Why is there a woman running around my table? Why is it a good idea? It’s a very good idea.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lap three! Everybody on the last one!

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: ...NO. I said no. Why is everyone in my kitchen? Is that a mother running laps with two little girls?

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: ...Okay. That one can stay.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That wasn’t a lap. That was a Tombo. Run With Us, Mommy. Amy, Grace and Rose, together.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: Take lemons. Take ALL the lemons. Every yard in this city has too many and somebody always leaves them on my step.

lines.speaker: Daisy
lines.text: Is it okay if I say that was the best thing that has ever happened in our kitchen?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It was the best thing in OUR kitchen too. We don’t even have a kitchen table. We have a counter.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Look at that. You put the neighbors back. Very warm. Very busy. Very much not what I asked for.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The rest of the colors too, please. All of them.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes. This intersection has no flow. Let me introduce our new Head of Traffic.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Mr. Prime! Please give them a moment to rethink the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s the biggest car in the WORLD.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Every light on the block is red. Every single one.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. Its headlights are pointed at the ground. It looks sad.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: It’s not angry. It’s stuck. Stuck is very quiet, and Mr. Vance likes quiet. Do be quick. The notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: If it’s stuck, maybe it just needs somewhere to go. Kindness first. Hit it if it hits back.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Here’s the plan. I stay with the girls. If anybody needs a break, sit on a couch or a bench and we’ll swap.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody gets run over. I’ll step in front of anyone who needs it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody okay? Good. It floors Rush Hour every third turn, so we heal before, not after.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: ...SigAlert cleared. Merging left. I’m sorry. Everybody was in my lane.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s fine. Nobody was in your lane. You were in everybody’s. Take the exit.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The green lamp just popped off the traffic light. It’s still warm, and it’s humming.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The pink is back! The jacaranda has its pink back!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the music is back in the window.

lines.speaker: Mr. Washington
lines.text: ...and that is why you never trust a Tuesday. Hm? Why is everybody looking at me? Did I fall asleep? Again?

lines.speaker: Larry
lines.text: I’m blowing leaves. The leaf landed. It LANDED. Thirty years I’ve waited. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Love it. Hate it. Love it. Notes withdrawn.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I’ll be Downtown, at the Movie Palace. Come by. I’ll have notes for the rest of the family.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Where is my mother?

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Long Island is under glass, you know. A very safe house. Your mother is in the kitchen. She’s making a crisp. She’s been making it for hours.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Tell me where.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Notes are due at five.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He just told us something he shouldn’t have.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Long Island is under glass. So we go under the glass. Or around it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal and Sol know every road between here and there. We start with the cab stand.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll get them back. We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sol. Sal says there’s a way under the dome. Tell me you know where.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Tom. Sit. Not that chair. That chair is Sal’s. I keep it warm for him out of spite.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Okay. Sal and I are cousins. You know that. What you don’t know is what we do between airport runs.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Is it crimes?

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Letters. Eleven years of letters, Snail Mail to Los Angeles, in the trunks of cabs. Nobody ever opened a bag. Nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a hundred sacks of stamps.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You’ve been running a secret mail route.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: A dispatch network. We call it the Network. We never came up with a better name.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Sol. Sol, come in. It’s Sal. Cab seven says hi. She’s fine. She’s the only thing in town that’s moving.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Sal. I have Tom, his sister, two nieces, a boyfriend and a dog in my lobby. Say hi.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Tommy! It’s quiet in here. Even the clocks are quiet. Your mother’s in the kitchen. Don’t panic. She’s fine. She just won’t stop baking.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal. Can you get me in?

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: I’m under the dome with a shovel and a very worried shopkeeper. I can’t get out. But I can dig toward you.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The Sub-Rail. Sal and I bored a tunnel under the Layover, from both coasts, for a hobby. It was supposed to open in 2031. It meets in the middle, right under the dome.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: You built a transcontinental subway. As a hobby.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: We got a very good deal on a drill.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The drill stopped answering when the dome came down. Something put a chip in it. Be careful of the worm.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The worm.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The drill. We call her the Dual-Coast Drill. The kids at the depot call her the Worm. She doesn’t love it.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: I need dispatchers. Two of them. Radio only. Somebody has to read me the tunnel.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I’m extremely good at being in charge.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m in charge of snacks.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. Dispatch is the most important job in the building. If Sol says stay, you stay.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Copy.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Copy copy.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Sol. I am leaving my children with a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Thirty years. Never lost a passenger. Found two in the trunk. Both were fine.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Somehow that is not comforting.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We’ll be on the radio the whole way. Grace, you’re the voice. Rose, you’re the snacks.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snacks are critical infrastructure.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB. Nara. Amy. With me. We go down.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have my thermos. I’m always ready for a tunnel.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara has never been this ready for anything. She is already at the Metro stairs, vibrating.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Out the door, the Metro stairs on the boulevard. Past the turnstile, there’s a door that says EMPLOYEES ONLY. That’s you. You’re employees now.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: EMPLOYEES ONLY. A platform under the boulevard. And a tunnel.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I have ridden every line in this city. I didn’t know this one existed. I’m a little bit offended.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. Radio check. Say “over.”

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Over.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: At the END, Tata. You say it at the end of what you say.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I said it at the end. It was the only thing I said.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Snack check! Check your pockets! I put a pretzel in your left one!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...There’s a pretzel in my left pocket.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Tom! Good. Okay. Before you go in, I have to tell you something, and I have to say it fast, because Penny made me promise.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nickel. You’re shaking.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: A man in a long coat bought gold coins from our shops. For years. Paid double. Never took his hat off.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Julian Vance.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: We didn’t know. We thought he was a collector. We took the money. And we kept the best coins in the back, in case he ever paid triple.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Penny called on the Network from under the dome. She said, “Tell Tom we’re sorry.” And then she said, “The drawer is under the counter.”

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Eleven coins. Hers and mine. The last of the old gold. They were supposed to be a retirement.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Why bring them?

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Sal says gold remembers being warm. If amber is warmth that got stuck, then gold can give it somewhere to go. He says. I don’t know. He’s a cab driver.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re giving up your retirement.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: I’m giving up a drawer. It’s the best drawer I ever had. Go. I’ll bring them down behind you. Sol’s driving me to the second mile marker and making me run.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You don’t have to do this.

lines.speaker: Nickel
lines.text: Yes, I do. Somebody gave me a shop. I’d like to be somebody who gave something back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The tracks run east. We follow the rails.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Stay together. Nobody falls behind. I’ll be counting.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re at mile marker one thousand two hundred and fifty. But the tunnel is forty feet long. Is that normal?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The sign says halfway. I’m choosing to believe the sign.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, did you see the stone in the doorway? It’s STANDING. I think it’s the bouncer.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Dispatch to Tom. You’re breaking up. Say... over... Tata?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata? I can’t hear the... Tata? Tata?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace? Rose? The radio’s gone. It’s not static. It’s just gone.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: THIS IS A QUIET CAR.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara barks. Nothing comes out. She tries again. Nothing. She looks at her own mouth, deeply offended.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Noise is a leak. Families are the loudest leak I have ever measured.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Who are you?

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: HUSH-9. Quiet Car, Series Nine. Property of Mr. Vance. Mr. Vance likes it quiet. Quiet is safe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That’s the second time today somebody has told me quiet is safe. Marlowe said it too.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: Marlowe takes the color. I take the sound. We are a very good team. Please lower your voices.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We’re being pretty quiet right now.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: You are breathing audibly.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I teach kids for a living. I know what a person sounds like right before they say “be quiet.” You’re in the wrong tunnel.

lines.speaker: HUSH-9
lines.text: I have given the Drill a chip. It no longer digs toward a place. It digs toward the noise. Please observe the quiet. Goodbye.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He left the quiet on. Is anybody else’s ears ringing?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The chip makes it listen for noise. So we make a lot of it. Loudly. Together.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I’ve been trying to get Rose to use her indoor voice for six years. I’m glad somebody finally wants her outdoor one.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A cavern. A wall of amber the size of a house. And a hole in the dirt exactly the width of a drill.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That is the biggest drill I have ever seen.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s a Dual-Coast Drill. They went with the budget model. I can tell by the bolts.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s not charging. It’s digging in place. Round and round.

lines.text: Hello, Tom. Thank you for flying nowhere. I have waited a very long time for a picture where nobody leaves.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That’s the voice. That’s the fella with the deal.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Hello, Robert. You broke our contract. That’s all right. I am a forgiving man. Everybody, please look here.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I’m doing my photo face.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m doing my ALSO face.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I know. Girls, down. Behind me. NOW.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Not Tom. Not the grown ones. The little ones. The ones with all their years still in them. Those are the ones I want to keep.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Robert.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I know.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Girls. Close your eyes. Moon and back.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Nobody gets past us.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom! Dad!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Fifty-one years.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...And counting.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy. You can move now.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody moves. Nobody says anything. In the middle of the Square two stone figures hold each other up, and a small amber light crawls along their joined hands.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: There. That is a family photograph. Thank you, Tom. You may keep the frame.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Where are you?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Marlowe. Collect the children.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Mr. Vance. They are... they are children. I only moved the colors around. That’s all I ever did. I never wrote anything like that.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Then I shall help with your notes.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: Less. Less. Less. That is all I ever wanted. Less.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace. Rose. Go. Cab seven. Find Sal. Now.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: But Deedee...

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. Go. Please, Grace.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose. Hand. Run. Now.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: But Boppy...

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I KNOW. RUN.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. Whatever this is, it is between them and the road.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then it doesn’t get past us. Dad said so.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’m here, babe.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara plants her feet in the grass and growls at a grey man with a sun behind his head.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Up. We are not done. Breathe. Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Up. We are not done. Breathe. Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The amber goes out of him all at once. Nobody cheers. There is no song. There is only the wind going through the Square.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I wanted it quieter. I only ever wanted it quieter.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Look at them. LOOK.

lines.speaker: Marlowe
lines.text: I didn’t want it like this.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nobody does. That is what he counts on.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom. Dad.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s warm. Amy. It’s still a little warm.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Then they’re not gone.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: They’re not gone.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Then we get them back.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Thank you for the photograph. It is perfect. I would like to keep it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Give them back.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Nobody leaves, Tom. That is what a photograph is for. If you want them, you know the building. Downtown. Sixty floors. Do come up. I will leave the light on.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: TOMMY! The glass is coming down! I have the girls in the cab! GET IN!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy. TNB. Nara. Run.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad. Keep her warm. I’m coming back.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sal took the Sub-Rail the long way, with the meter off. Nobody has said anything since the tunnel.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. Are they cold?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No, Rose. They’re warm. I checked.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Then it’s not forever. It’s just a long time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It’s just a long time.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Vance said downtown. Sixty floors. We rest tonight. Tomorrow we go up.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Downtown. The tallest thing on the boulevard that wasn’t there on Monday. Sixty floors of glass, and every clock in it says 4:59.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That’s the building. That’s where he is.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We’re coming. All of us. I already told Rose. She’s packing.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I packed a pretzel. And a second pretzel, for Deedee.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Girls. It is sixty floors. It is going to be hard and strange and not fair.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We know. That’s why we’re coming.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. Here’s how we do it. Two teams of three. Grace, Rose and me take the stairs. Amy, TNB and Nara work the Archive on thirty.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Divide and conquer. I like it. I also like not being on the stairs.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara does not like stairs. Nara is, however, extremely good at breaking glass.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: And I get to hit something. Good.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: I’ll keep the meter off and the engine on. Go get your folks, Tommy.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The tower goes up past the top of the screen. The doors at the bottom are glass, and they are glowing like a lit window at dinnertime.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It’s so tall. Tata, it’s TALLER than the Starlite.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The lobby is all glass and no people. Every clock says 4:59. The second hands are shaking in place, like they are trying very hard.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s so clean. Nobody lives here. Nobody even touched the floor.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s a plant. It looks scared.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Floor directory says the stairs are on the east side. Twenty-eight flights.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Twenty-eight? That’s a leg day AND an arm day.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The lifts are locked. We take the stairs to thirty. Amy, TNB and Nara meet us up there.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Landing thirty. A huge glass door with a gold lock the size of a dinner plate. The counter over it says LOCKS ENGAGED 6 OF 6.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Six locks. Six of something. I don’t like that.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom, this is Amy. We’re in the service ducts. I can hear glass. A lot of glass. There’s a little hatch on your landing, it should open on the Archive.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Found it. Staff only. Somebody wrote HE IS OBVIOUSLY STAFF under it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That’s TNB’s handwriting. Go through. Girls hold the landing.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Holding the landing! Holding it! Holding!

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Attention. A collection has been disturbed. Six exhibits are no longer on file.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: This is unfortunate. This is not a problem. The Archivist is not unkind. The Archivist is only thorough.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Floors 2 to 30 are now unlocked for your convenience. The express lift has been withdrawn. Please use the stairs. All of them. The Archivist will be waiting at the top.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Withdrawn. The lift has been WITHDRAWN. Tom. Did he just challenge me to a stair race?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I don’t think he knows what he just did.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The seal door swings open on its own. The stairwell goes on. Twenty-nine more floors, straight up, in a glass tube.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You and me. Landing to landing. Loser buys dinner.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Amy, we have a deadline. We have a tower. We have two grandparents made of stone.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Which is why I am going to win this.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I am calling it. On my mark. Mark!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I’m the finish line!

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I am not running. I am carrying the thermos. Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Floor fifty-nine. We hit the vault door at exactly the same time. Amy’s forehead and mine, a quarter inch apart.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: That was MINE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It was a tie.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tie means nobody won. Tie means I lost. Rematch. Later. After.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: After.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The Vault. One plinth, one snow globe, and a view of Los Angeles at 4:59 PM, golden and perfect and completely still.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. It’s the Square. It’s in there. That’s Deedee. That’s BOPPY.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They’re so small. They’re okay. They’re holding hands.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay behind me. All of you.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Thank you for the six exhibits. The collection is, for the first time, incomplete. I find that I do not like it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You’re the Archivist.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: I am what Mr. Vance keeps when he wants a thing never to change. I file. I label. I hold. It is all I was made to do. It is a very good job.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You froze the pierogi man for thirty years.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Thirty-one. He was very happy. I made sure of it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That is the single saddest thing I have ever heard a lens say.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: Please hold still. This will not hurt. Nothing will, ever again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everyone up. We have a lens to break. Breathe. Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Up. Everyone up. We have a lens to break. Breathe. Then we go again.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The amber lens cracks across the middle. The cold one goes dark. For one second, the whole building holds its breath.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: I was only... keeping them safe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. They were never yours to keep.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: What does one do... with a day that is allowed to end?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: You eat dinner. Then you go to sleep. Then it’s morning.

lines.speaker: Archivist
lines.text: That sounds... sufficient.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. The globe.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The snow globe on the plinth lifts an inch off the glass. The gold cable above it goes tight. It is going up.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Thank you for the tour, Tom. Thank you for the Archive. It was very nearly complete.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Floor sixty is for family. Come up when you are ready. I have kept your parents very warm.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. Dad. We are coming. We’re coming.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody breathe. We rest. Then we go to the top.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A gold lift door stands open at the north wall. No call button. A brass plate: FLOOR 60. BY INVITATION.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The pinnacle lift opens without a sound. There is no button inside, no floor number. The walls are mirrors, and every one of us is in them.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody in. Nobody lags behind. Nobody gets left on this floor.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. I’m scared. I’m also coming. Both of those are true at the same time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That is exactly the right amount of both.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I brought a pretzel for Deedee. It’s a little bit squished.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Squished is fine. I fix squished things for a living.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stay behind me. All of you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The lift opens on a round room made of clock. Gold thread runs floor to ceiling, thousands of strands, humming. In the middle stands a loom the size of a house. In front of it, a man in a long coat has his back to us. His hat is on.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. Thank you for coming. Everyone, please, come in. Mind the threads. They are all somebody’s afternoon.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Where are my parents.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Warm. Downstairs, on a plinth, under glass. Exactly as you left them. I want you to understand I have taken very good care of them.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They’re STONE.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: They are safe. There is a difference. I had to have it explained to me, too.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Are you the man who took all the coins?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I am the man who kept them. Gold remembers being warm. I only wanted it to keep remembering.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. I fix things for a living. Whatever this is, it is structurally unsound.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Nothing is the same twice, Mr. TNB. You mend a cup, and it is a mended cup. I would like every cup to stay unbroken.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That is not how cups work.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. You know why I wanted you. Two places that kept moving, and one man flying between them. You are not a traveler. You are the thread. If you stop, they stop. If you stay, they stay.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I will not hurt you. I will not hurt anyone. I will only finish the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No, thank you. We have a connection to make.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I know. That is why this is so hard.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The threads of the Loom lean. All of them, all at once, like a field in the wind. They gather into the brass lens at the end of his arm.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: The Ray unwrites whatever it touches. It is very gentle. They will not remember being sad. Mrs. Gregori. Mr. TNB. Grace. Rose. Hold hands, please.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Over my dead body.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: That will not be necessary. That is not even on the table.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Girls. Amy. TNB. Nara. Behind me.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara presses herself against the back of Tom’s legs and does not make a sound. She is very good at this.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He adjusts his glasses. He has done it before every hard thing, his whole life. Then he raises one hand, palm out, and takes one step forward.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No touching, please.

lines.speaker: Floor 60
lines.text: Where Tom was standing, there is a small warm light, hanging in the air at about the height of his glasses. Then there is not.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. TATA.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He was right there. He was RIGHT there.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara walks to the exact spot where Tom was standing, lies down on it, and does not move.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Tom. Tom, answer me. I am not doing this. I am not doing this.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Tom.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: That was not in the model.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: The Ray was written for five. He took all of it. I did not think anyone would step into it. I have never once seen anyone step into it.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Give him back.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I cannot. The Loom does not hand back. I only know how it keeps.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: He is not destroyed. The Ray unwrites the story of a thing. Somewhere he is still a man with a thermos. The Loom simply does not have a place to put him.

lines.speaker: Floor 60
lines.text: The Loom shudders. Every thread in it goes white. The Ray has nowhere left to go, and a wave of light rolls out from the place Tom stood.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: It will take you home. It goes where he is from. Hold on to something.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: We are not leaving without him!

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: You are not leaving. You are being sent. That is a different thing.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Okay. We are on Second Avenue. It is morning. It is somehow morning.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is Tata coming?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He said we always make our connection. So he will.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: I know my brother. He is going to turn up late, a little annoyed, with a full explanation, and ask if anybody ate.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: His thermos is on the porch rail. He left it out for the cat.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is the cat going to be okay?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The cat is fine. The cat is always fine. The cat is not even his.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara sits down on Tom’s porch step, facing the street, and waits.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Okay. Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere. And there is exactly one thing in this city that does not forget where things go.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The post office.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: I’ll make coffee first. Tom would want me to make coffee first.
