lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It has been eleven hours. I have made coffee four times. I have not drunk any of it. That is not like me.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere the Loom does not have a place for. And there is one place in this city that keeps everything nobody could put anywhere.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The post office. We already said that.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Nara found it first.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara is sitting very straight in front of Tom’s mailbox, and she is staring into the slot. She has not blinked. A thin gold light is coming out of the slot, like a sleeping lamp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That is not a regular mailbox. That is a mailbox that is thinking about something.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: It’s his. It’s the mailbox at the bottom of his steps, where his bills and my birthday cards go. It’s warm.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: If you drop a letter in a mailbox and it goes nowhere... where does it go?

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Down. I think it goes down.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Whoa. It’s a post office for things that don’t have anywhere to go.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Dead letters. Every undelivered thing in the city ends up under it. Birthday cards. Thank-you notes. One pretzel.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That’s MY pretzel. I mean Rose’s. Rose’s pretzel. For Deedee.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Look at the big ledger. There’s a page for Second Avenue. There’s a blank rectangle where a name should be.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It’s still wet. Somebody erased him and left the space, like they were going to write somebody else in.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Four doors. One for each of us.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: People who would not forget him. That’s the whole job description.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The desk in the middle has four little brass niches in the front. Four of us, four niches. And a chair that someone just stood up out of.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There’s a thermos on it.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: That’s his. I would know that thermos in the dark.

lines.speaker: Dead-Letter Office
lines.text: Four keepsakes glow in four brass niches. The bell sits on the counter. Rose reaches up, stands on her tiptoes, and rings it.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Good evening. The Office is closed. May I help you? You look lost, which is the right way to look in here.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: We’re here for a name. A man named Tom, on Second Avenue.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I have one clean line on a page. I have a name that is too loud for it. I was tidying. It is not personal. I tidy everything that does not fit.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He is my brother.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I am sure he is lovely. He is also unclaimed. Everything here is. That is the best a thing can be, Mrs. Gregori: safe and unclaimed.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can’t erase somebody because he doesn’t fit your form.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is the only thing I am for. No one has ever handed me a letter to deliver. They only hand me returns.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: That’s the saddest job in the world.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is a very tidy job.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Please step back from the desk. I will write the name out.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. We can do this again. It’s a pottery rule: the first one always cracks.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. We can do this again. It’s a pottery rule: the first one always cracks.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: The Censor lowers his stamp. The black bar over his face slides to the side, a little at a time, and under it is only a small tired man with ink on his cuffs.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I have never been argued with by so many people at once. It was... full.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sorry I was late. I was written out of the schedule. I’ll sort it out with accounting.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: TATA!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: TATA!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello. Hello. Yes. Careful of the glasses. The glasses have been through a lot.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: You absolute marshmallow. You were GONE. You ate nothing. You skipped lunch for a whole afternoon, and then a night.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I had a granola bar. It was written out too. I haven’t felt this hungry since the nineties.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara arrives at about a hundred miles an hour and climbs directly onto Tom. Nobody tries to stop her.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. I know. I missed you too. I was a small gold light and I missed you the whole time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He turns to the Censor, who is looking at the floor.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You have never delivered anything.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Rose.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Here. It’s a little bit squished. It’s for Deedee. It was held for pickup, but nobody picked it up, because she’s stone.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It is a first-timer’s route. One pretzel. One tower. Fifty-nine floors up, and then a grandmother.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I do not... I have never left the Office.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The route is not far. The job is only to put a thing in someone’s hands. You are already very good at the part where you carry it.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: The Censor takes the pretzel in both hands, carefully, as if it were made of glass. Then he lifts his stamp, looks at it, and brings it down on the napkin. It does not say RETURN TO SENDER. It says DELIVERED.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: It is a nicer word to hold than I expected.

lines.speaker: Dead-Letter Office
lines.text: In the big ledger, the clean white rectangle fills itself in, one slow letter at a time. T. O. M. The ink is the exact blue of a thermos cap.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Okay. Home. Food. Then Mom and Dad. In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Stone does not respond to talking. I have checked. Stone responds to being warm for a long time with people nearby.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom’s rule: a house is warm when somebody is cooking in it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So we cook.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: A lot. We cook a LOT.

lines.speaker: Olivia
lines.text: Tom! You’re BACK. I saw the light on at four a.m. and I thought, he’s home, and then I thought, no, that’s a different kind of light. I made a lasagna.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: I brought a rock. Lachlan picked it out. Isla ate a different rock. We are keeping a close eye on it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you. All of you. I will put the rock on the mantel.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Alvarez
lines.text: I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. And peppers. My nephew grows them. They are very hot. A man called Boppy would know what to do.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Boppy would eat one raw and say it was “fine” in a voice.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The kitchen is a mess. Every pot is in use. The window is fogged. It smells like a Sunday.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: The oven door handle came off. I fixed it. You could say I handled it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Please stop.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Lasagna, eleven minutes. Lemon bars, six. I have a timer on everything. Nobody is allowed to be late for this.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I choreographed the pasta. It goes from the pot to the plate in a very specific arc.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I am the taster. I have tasted nine times. It’s for quality.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The pasta does not go in an arc.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It goes in an arc if you believe in it, Tata.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He looks at the table. Everyone he loves is crowded around it, and somebody has put a rock in the middle like a centerpiece. He doesn’t say anything for a second.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Pack it up. Sal is waiting outside with cab seven. We are going to the Glass Tower, and we are bringing dinner.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in. Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I am not even charging. I am scared of that tower and I am going anyway.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The snow globe is still on its plinth. Inside it, very small, two stone figures hold each other up. The amber light is crawling on their hands. It is slower than before.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom. Dad. We brought dinner.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I brought a pretzel. It has been DELIVERED. It has a stamp.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Everybody sit. Around the plinth. Nobody leave. Plates on laps.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Steam from the lasagna drifts across the glass. The amber light turns the color of toast. A crack of warm yellow runs along the stone, then two, then nine.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It’s working. It’s working!

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Oh. Oh, my back. My back is going to be talking about this for a week.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is that lasagna? Who made lasagna? Who has been in my kitchen?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: DEEDEE! BOPPY!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Oh, my babies. Come here. All of you. Come here, to the moon and back and back and back.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Which one of you is eating the peppers raw?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Nobody. Yet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Hand me one. For my knees.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everyone is crowded onto one floor of a glass tower with plates in their laps, and for a minute, it is just a family having dinner, eight people and a dog.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom. Who is the man in the gold coat? The one who kept us on a shelf?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Vance. He is still up there, at the top. He is going to want more than a shelf.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then we finish eating first.

lines.speaker: Floor 59
lines.text: Overhead, through the glass ceiling, every clock in the sky stops. They are all pointing at the same minute: the one just after the last. A door nobody has noticed before, high up in the tower, has begun to open.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He sets down his plate. Then he picks it back up.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Seconds first. Then the sky.

lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: Eight lamps light round the frame of the lift in the middle of the Core, one for each of you. The brass doors slide apart, and a warm gold light comes out of the shaft.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He built a lock that opens for family. All eight of us, and a thermos. I resent how much I admire that.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: The Extra Place. Mom set a place for everybody at every dinner for fifty years. That is the whole trick. He should have asked her.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is it ready? Because I made a lot.

lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: THE EXTRA PLACE (the all-eight Family Finish) is ready. It costs 75% HEART.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: In the ceiling of the Vault, a round brass door has opened. It has a clock for a keyhole. It is ticking very slowly, like a heart that has been told to be quiet.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: That is the biggest clock I have ever seen. And I have a lot of clocks. They all run fast, for my stomach.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Is that the man’s house? Somebody should tell him to leave a light on.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Everybody stays together. All eight. Nobody goes through a door alone.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We always make our connection.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Nara goes first. She is the best at doors.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Eight of us, a dog and a thermos. Seconds first, then the sky. Let us go.

lines.speaker: Stillness Core
lines.text: The lift opens into a round chamber of brass and glass, behind the face of the sky clock. Every wall is a gear, and every gear is turning very slowly. Eight round doors stand sealed around a lift in the middle. Each keyhole is shaped like somebody.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I get a door too?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You get a door too.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: It is a very good lock. Whoever made it really cared about the mechanism.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: One skill each. Whatever you are best at, that is your door.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: A column of gears the height of a tower. Around it, a brass serpent as long as a street is slowly uncoiling. Every scale is a clock face. Every clock says 4:59. At the top of the Engine, on a platform of glass, a man in a long coat stands with his back to you.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Tom. You came back. You always come back. That is the thing I could never forgive you for.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I was written out of the schedule. I am a very stubborn calendar entry.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Everything leaves. Time takes a little every day, and then one day all of it. So I built a place where it cannot. The Leviathan keeps every afternoon exactly as it was. Please do not hurt it. It is all I have.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You turned my grandparents into STATUES.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I kept them safe.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I was a statue for a week and my back did not get a single day off. I would like to file a complaint.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Julian, honey. Have you eaten?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: There are four things that will keep you out. Distance. Age. Exhaustion. Fear. Four things I could never get past. You will not, either.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Distance, age, exhaustion, fear. That is just a regular Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Okay. Four barriers. We have a plan for every one of them. Everybody ready?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is the snake going to be mean?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It is going to be very, very tired. Be kind about it, and be fast.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: The Chronos-Leviathan lowers its head. Every clock on its body ticks at once.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. It is a long fight, and we are a long family. We can do this again.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. It is a long fight, and we are a long family. We can do this again.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: The Leviathan comes apart. It does not die. It comes apart like a watch being taken out of its case, one gear at a time, every one of them still ticking.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: Where its coil was, there is a room made of glass. A small living room. One lamp, one armchair. A man in a long coat is sitting in it with his hat in his hands. He is a good deal smaller than the shadow he threw.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: My daughter was nine. I was on a flight. I told her, one more flight next month. It was her birthday. I told my mother the same thing, about the hospital. I told my partner the same thing about everything.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: There was always one more flight next month. And then there was not. So I stopped the months. I did not know how to say goodbye. So I made sure that nobody could leave.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Julian.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Eternal Silence.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: Every sound in the Engine goes out. Every move you have turns to grey stone, and the stone falls and lies on the glass floor. He did not fight. He only went quiet, and asked everyone to.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: He is not attacking us. Look at his hands.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: They are shaking.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is he cold?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No hitting. He has done enough to everybody else. Do the thing you are each best at, for him. Everybody. In turn. I will be last.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The last one is always the hardest. That is why I put the pepper first.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody up. He is not going anywhere. That is rather the point of him.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Everybody up. He is not going anywhere. That is rather the point of him.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: Julian is still in the armchair. He has a cardigan on and a tennis ball in his lap, and a plate of rhubarb crisp that he has not eaten. The glass of the living room is cracked right down the middle, and every crack is letting the light in.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: Clara would be thirty-one. She would say I deserved all of this.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Probably. And then she would sit down next to you anyway.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I could not make the minute stop hurting. So I stopped the minute. It did not stop hurting. It only stopped.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Honey. That is all of it. That is what living is. It hurts a little, every time, and you do it anyway.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And the crisp is excellent.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I do not know how to start the clocks.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You do not start them. You stop holding them.

lines.speaker: Forever Engine
lines.text: Julian lets go. A long breath goes out of him, the one that has been in him for twenty years. The Forever Engine lets go with him. One by one, every gear in the Moon begins to turn the right way, and far below, in two cities, every clock in the sky ticks forward, all together, to five o’clock.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: IT MOVED! The clock MOVED!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It is five o’clock. It is just five o’clock. It is the best five o’clock I have ever seen.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: The towns in the Archive are open. The coins are going home. The snow globe is a town again. I am sorry. I do not know how to say how sorry.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You are doing it right now. Come to dinner.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I do not have anything to bring.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Bring yourself and an appetite.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: And bring a chair. We are short a chair.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Mom already set the place. She set it at every dinner for fifty years. There is always one more seat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Long Island is a town again. The fountain is running. The library door is open. Someone has already started a pie, which is how you know it is real.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Look! Look who is delivering!

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Good afternoon. I have four parcels. This is the first delivery I have ever made. Please do not be too nice about it. I am a little emotional.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: My squishy! The Sparkling Diamond Gold Soup Dumpling squishy!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: My pink ribbon! It is still tied in a bow!

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: My stopwatch. It is still running. It is at nine hundred and eleven hours, and some seconds.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: My first cup. It is full. It is still warm. I do not know how that is possible and I am not going to ask.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: Each one is stamped DELIVERED. It is, I have learned, my favorite word.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He hands me a fifth parcel. It is small and brown. It is addressed, in my own handwriting, to Tom, Second Avenue. It is a letter I never mailed.

lines.speaker: Oblivion Censor
lines.text: I did not open it. That is not my department anymore. I only deliver.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in! I am not charging. I am not even driving. Look UP.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: High over the Square, a line of gold runs from the sky down to the fountain. There is a rail on it with a seam of bright gold, exactly where somebody mended it. A train glides in, quiet as a held breath. The sign on its front says LONG ISLAND on one side and LOS ANGELES on the other.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I made it from the Engine. It runs both coasts. It does not stop the clocks. It only makes the distance a little shorter. I thought, if I had built that first...

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You would have been home for the birthday.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I would have been home.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: A SKYWAY TRAIN?! I do not know what to do with my hands! I am a cab driver!

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: You are the first passenger. Get in the train.

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.text: Three thousand miles. One ride. Mom, Dad, you can come to Tom’s any Tuesday you like.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Does it have a recliner?

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: It has four. I asked.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I have changed my mind about the man.

lines.speaker: Vance
lines.text: I am going to call my daughter. I do not know whether she will pick up. I am going to call anyway.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That is a good seat to start in.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A week later. Jefferson Park, six in the evening. The street light has come on, and for once it is not worth mentioning.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata, the train came again. It has a snack cart. It has a snack CART.

lines.speaker: Grace

lines.text: Round {n}. I am heavier when wet. I am always wet.

lines.speaker: Snag
lines.text: ...Zzz. Everyone gets caught on me. Nobody stays.

lines.speaker: Snag
lines.text: I'm soaking. I'm always soaking.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: BLORP. I'm older than the pier. I'm older than the old man.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Every hook in this marsh has been in my lip once. I spat them all out.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. I'm still burping peppers.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Round {n}. Bring the old man. I miss him.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: Blorp. That pepper jar is still repeating on me.

lines.speaker: Old Iron-Gill
lines.text: The pool is deep. I'll be at the bottom of it.

lines.speaker: Extra Extra
lines.text: I've been an extra in forty movies. You've seen the back of my head forty times.

lines.speaker: Extra Extra
lines.text: They said there'd be a hot lunch. It was a cold sandwich.

lines.speaker: Extra Extra
lines.text: I'm back. They reset the scene.

lines.speaker: Extra Extra
lines.text: Round {n}. I got a new coat. Same coat, actually.

lines.speaker: Extra Extra
lines.text: ...Nine hours in holding. Nine.

lines.speaker: Extra Extra
lines.text: I'm Man in Coat Number Four. They never call Number Four.

lines.speaker: Boom Mic Moth
lines.text: I hang over everybody all day. Nobody looks up. Nobody says thank you.

lines.speaker: Boom Mic Moth
lines.text: Every time someone says CUT, I'm the last to know.

lines.speaker: Boom Mic Moth
lines.text: Bzzz. I'm back in frame.

lines.speaker: Boom Mic Moth
lines.text: Round {n}. I can hear you breathing.

lines.speaker: Boom Mic Moth
lines.text: ...Fuzz. I'm fuzzy. Leave me alone.

lines.speaker: Boom Mic Moth
lines.text: I hear everything. EVERYTHING. It's a lot.

lines.speaker: Clapper Snapper
lines.text: SNAP. I go first. I ALWAYS go first. Nothing happens until I clap.

lines.speaker: Clapper Snapper
lines.text: Every take starts with me and nobody remembers me.

lines.speaker: Clapper Snapper
lines.text: Take two! Snap!

lines.speaker: Clapper Snapper
lines.text: Round {n}. Rolling. Speed. SNAP.

lines.speaker: Clapper Snapper
lines.text: ...Snap. I'm resting between takes.

lines.speaker: Clapper Snapper
lines.text: Scene four, take nine. Don't ask about the other eight.

lines.speaker: Fog Wisp
lines.text: Everything looks better in fog. Mysterious. Soft. Nobody can see anybody.

lines.speaker: Fog Wisp
lines.text: They pump me in and then they open the doors. Every time.

lines.speaker: Fog Wisp
lines.text: Back again. Thicker.

lines.speaker: Fog Wisp
lines.text: Round {n}. Can you see me? No. Good.

lines.speaker: Fog Wisp
lines.text: ...Hazy. I'm feeling hazy.

lines.speaker: Fog Wisp
lines.text: Don't look at me. You can't see me anyway.

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: I hold up the lines. Every line. Nobody ever says "nice handwriting."

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: Pinch. I wrote that one myself.

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: New cards. Same feelings.

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: Round {n}. This card says ROUND {n}.

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: ...I'm rewriting my cards.

lines.speaker: Cue Card Crab
lines.text: Nobody reads my cards. They read the actors.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: CUT! CUT! Again! The light was wrong! The FEELING was wrong!

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: Forty years of bad takes. I've heard every one of them. Through me.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: From the top!

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: Round {n}. Take {n}. Still wrong.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: ...From the top. Again. Always from the top.

lines.speaker: The Director’s Cut
lines.text: Nobody gets it right. NOBODY.

lines.speaker: Pop Quiz
lines.text: Nobody ever studies for me. That's the whole point of me. It's still rude.

lines.speaker: Pop Quiz
lines.text: I have nine questions and one of them is a trick.

lines.speaker: Pop Quiz
lines.text: Retake! Pencils up!

lines.speaker: Pop Quiz
lines.text: Round {n}. Question {n}. Show your work.

lines.speaker: Pop Quiz
lines.text: ...I'm all multiple choice inside.

lines.speaker: Pop Quiz
lines.text: The answer is C. The answer is always C.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: Everybody groans when I ring. Every single time. For forty years.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: I'm not the one who's late. I'm just the one who says so.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: Ding ding! Round two!

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: Round {n}. You are late for round {n}.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: ...Ding. Quietly. Ding.

lines.speaker: Tardy Bell
lines.text: I ring on time. Everybody else is late.

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: Kids use me for one art project and then I sit in a drawer for three years.

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: I'm not messy. I'm DECORATIVE.

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: Still sticky!

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: Round {n}. Even stickier.

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: ...Drying. Don't touch me. I'm drying.

lines.speaker: Glitter Glue
lines.text: You'll be finding me in your hair until June.

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: Every kid in this school is scared of me. I didn't ask for that.

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: I just want to be picked first. Once.

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: Back in the game!

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: Round {n}. Still not picked.

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: ...Boing. I'm resting. Boing.

lines.speaker: Dodgeball Dread
lines.text: Nobody picks me. They just throw me.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: A hundred thousand wrong answers. I marked every single one.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Neatness counts. Nobody counts it. I count it.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Retake! From the top!

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Round {n}. Still a C minus.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: ...Points off. Points off for everybody.

lines.speaker: The Red Pen
lines.text: Nobody gets a hundred. NOBODY.

lines.speaker: Acorn Agent
lines.text: I'm just an acorn. With sunglasses. That's all you need to know.

lines.speaker: Acorn Agent
lines.text: The Chairman sees everything. Mostly from the tree.

lines.speaker: Acorn Agent
lines.text: Agents, regroup!

lines.speaker: Acorn Agent
lines.text: Round {n}. Over.

lines.speaker: Acorn Agent
lines.text: ...Copy that. Over.

lines.speaker: Acorn Agent
lines.text: You didn't see me. I was never here.

lines.speaker: Sticky Sap
lines.text: Everybody touches the tree and then says EW. I'm the tree.

lines.speaker: Sticky Sap
lines.text: I'm not sticky. I'm committed.

lines.speaker: Sticky Sap
lines.text: Still oozing!

lines.speaker: Sticky Sap
lines.text: Round {n}. Stickier.

lines.speaker: Sticky Sap
lines.text: ...Ooze. Ooze.

lines.speaker: Sticky Sap
lines.text: Give me a hundred years. I'll be amber.

lines.speaker: Peanut Gallery
lines.text: Nobody ever cheers for the peanut. They just crack us open.

lines.speaker: Peanut Gallery
lines.text: I boo because nobody ever asks what I think.

lines.speaker: Peanut Gallery
lines.text: Boo! Round two!

lines.speaker: Peanut Gallery
lines.text: Round {n}. Still booing.

lines.speaker: Peanut Gallery
lines.text: ...Boo. Quietly. Boo.

lines.speaker: Peanut Gallery
lines.text: I have notes. I always have notes.

lines.speaker: Twig Spy
lines.text: Code name: Twig. I report to the Chairman. Pretend I said nothing.

lines.speaker: Twig Spy
lines.text: Nobody looks twice at a stick. That's the job. It's lonely.

lines.speaker: Twig Spy
lines.text: Back on the stakeout!

lines.speaker: Twig Spy
lines.text: Round {n}. Still watching.

lines.speaker: Twig Spy
lines.text: ...I am a stick.

lines.speaker: Twig Spy
lines.text: Report to the Chairman: they're very tall.

lines.speaker: Cheek Stuffer
lines.text: Mmmf. (Winter is coming. Winter is ALWAYS coming.)

lines.speaker: Cheek Stuffer
lines.text: Mmf mmf mmf. (Nobody ever shares with a squirrel.)

lines.speaker: Cheek Stuffer
lines.text: Mmmf! Round two!

lines.speaker: Cheek Stuffer
lines.text: Round {n}. Mmf.

lines.speaker: Cheek Stuffer
lines.text: ...Mmmf.

lines.speaker: Cheek Stuffer
lines.text: Mmf mmf. (Winter is coming.)

lines.speaker: Acorn Cache
lines.text: ...It's an acorn.

lines.speaker: Acorn Cache
lines.text: ...It's an acorn.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: Every shiny thing on 2nd Avenue comes up this tree. Because winter is coming.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: Nobody shares with a squirrel. So the squirrel takes.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: ORDER! Round two!

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: Round {n}. Meeting is still in session.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: ...Order. Order.

lines.speaker: Chairman Cheeks
lines.text: Winter is coming. Write that down.

lines.speaker: Shusher
lines.text: Everybody uses me and then forgets which page I was on.

lines.speaker: Shusher
lines.text: Shh. The books are listening. They're ALWAYS listening.

lines.speaker: Shusher
lines.text: SHHHH! Again!

lines.speaker: Shusher
lines.text: Round {n}. Quietly. SHHH.

lines.speaker: Shusher
lines.text: ...shhh. Shhhh. Shh.

lines.speaker: Shusher
lines.text: I mark your place. Nobody marks mine.

lines.speaker: Dog-Ear
lines.text: I'm the corner of page 212. Somebody stopped reading here in 1987.

lines.speaker: Dog-Ear
lines.text: Nobody ever came back to finish. I've been folded for forty years.

lines.speaker: Dog-Ear
lines.text: Unfolded! Round two!

lines.speaker: Dog-Ear
lines.text: Round {n}. Still creased.

lines.speaker: Dog-Ear
lines.text: ...somebody folded me. Somebody always folds me.

lines.speaker: Dog-Ear
lines.text: Use a bookmark. That's all I ask. A BOOKMARK.

lines.speaker: The Cliffhanger
lines.text: Nobody ever finishes me. They read the first chapter and put me back. Every time.

lines.speaker: The Cliffhanger
lines.text: And then the uncle turned around and saw... no. I won't say.

lines.speaker: The Cliffhanger
lines.text: Previously, on this fight...

lines.speaker: The Cliffhanger
lines.text: Round {n}. And then... and then...

lines.speaker: The Cliffhanger
lines.text: ...and then... and THEN...

lines.speaker: The Cliffhanger
lines.text: Find out next time. Same shelf. Same book.

lines.speaker: The Know-It-All
lines.text: Nobody looks things up anymore. They just ask their phones. Their phones are WRONG.

lines.speaker: The Know-It-All
lines.text: Kangaroo. Kettle. Kindness. I know them all. Nobody asks.

lines.speaker: The Know-It-All
lines.text: Correction! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Know-It-All
lines.text: Round {n}. Footnote {n}.

lines.speaker: The Know-It-All
lines.text: ...actually. Actually. Ac-tu-al-ly.

lines.speaker: The Know-It-All
lines.text: I'm volume K. I know everything that starts with K.

lines.speaker: Pop-Up Panic
lines.text: Kids open me and scream. Then they laugh. Then they open me again. I love it.

lines.speaker: Pop-Up Panic
lines.text: Nobody opens me anymore. I've been ready to pop for six years.

lines.speaker: Pop-Up Panic
lines.text: BOO! Again!

lines.speaker: Pop-Up Panic
lines.text: Round {n}. Surprise!

lines.speaker: Pop-Up Panic
lines.text: ...boo. Boo? No? Nobody?

lines.speaker: Pop-Up Panic
lines.text: I'm supposed to be the surprise.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Seventy years on this shelf. Nobody has opened me once.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: You hear things, when nobody reads you. You hear EVERYTHING.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Chapter two. Again.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Round {n}. Page {n}.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: ...nobody. Not once. Since 1952.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: I know what you whispered. I know what everybody whispered.

lines.speaker: Lukewarm
lines.text: Nobody ever finishes me. They pour me, they get busy, they forget.

lines.speaker: Lukewarm
lines.text: I'm fine. I'm FINE. I'm exactly room temperature.

lines.speaker: Lukewarm
lines.text: Reheated! Round two!

lines.speaker: Lukewarm
lines.text: Round {n}. Still lukewarm.

lines.speaker: Lukewarm
lines.text: ...somebody made me and walked away.

lines.speaker: Lukewarm
lines.text: I was hot once. For about four minutes.

lines.speaker: Leftover
lines.text: Everybody brings me home. Nobody ever opens me again.

lines.speaker: Leftover
lines.text: Don't smell me. I'm serious. Don't.

lines.speaker: Leftover
lines.text: Reheated! Round two!

lines.speaker: Leftover
lines.text: Round {n}. Day {n} in the fridge.

lines.speaker: Leftover
lines.text: ...I was a lasagna. I think. Once.

lines.speaker: Leftover
lines.text: Somebody said they'd eat me tomorrow. That was a long tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Wet Blanket
lines.text: They used to throw me over the sparks when the welders worked. I put out every fire in this barn.

lines.speaker: Wet Blanket
lines.text: Now there's nothing left to put out. So I put out the fun.

lines.speaker: Wet Blanket
lines.text: Why bother? Round two.

lines.speaker: Wet Blanket
lines.text: Round {n}. Still damp.

lines.speaker: Wet Blanket
lines.text: ...why bother. Why bother at all.

lines.speaker: Wet Blanket
lines.text: Every spark in here, I put it out. Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: The Draft
lines.text: I blew out every pilot light on 2nd Avenue. Pfft. Pfft. Pfft. Very satisfying.

lines.speaker: The Draft
lines.text: Ironbelly asked for the flames. I just carried them. I'm a delivery draft.

lines.speaker: The Draft
lines.text: Woooo! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Draft
lines.text: Round {n}. Still drafty.

lines.speaker: The Draft
lines.text: ...wooo. Wooooo. That's me. I'm the wooo.

lines.speaker: The Draft
lines.text: Close a window. Go on. I'll find another one.

lines.speaker: The Picky Eater
lines.text: I don't eat cold food. I don't eat hot food. I don't eat food that TOUCHES.

lines.speaker: The Picky Eater
lines.text: Ironbelly used to warm every lunch in here. Now everything is cold, and everything is EW.

lines.speaker: The Picky Eater
lines.text: Ew! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Picky Eater
lines.text: Round {n}. Still not eating it.

lines.speaker: The Picky Eater
lines.text: ...ew. Ew. Is that touching? It's touching. EW.

lines.speaker: The Picky Eater
lines.text: I only eat the crust. No, the middle. No. Neither.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Biscuits for the night crew. Cornbread on Fridays. Every night from 1912 to 1963.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Everybody has a little fire upstairs. I only borrowed it.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Stoke it! Round two!

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Round {n}. Still preheating.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: ...cold. Sixty years cold.

lines.speaker: Old Ironbelly
lines.text: Nobody bakes anything anymore. Not in me.

lines.speaker: Velvet Rope
lines.text: Nobody has come to the door since 1971. I have kept the line VERY tidy.

lines.speaker: Velvet Rope
lines.text: I hold everyone back. Nobody ever asks to go in with me.

lines.speaker: Velvet Rope
lines.text: Back of the line! Round two!

lines.speaker: Velvet Rope
lines.text: Round {n}. Still not on the list.

lines.speaker: Velvet Rope
lines.text: ...name? Your name. It's not here.

lines.speaker: Velvet Rope
lines.text: The list. Everybody wants to be on the list.

lines.speaker: Stuffed Shirt
lines.text: Black tie. Black TIE. Is that a fishing vest? At the Moon Club?

lines.speaker: Stuffed Shirt
lines.text: Nobody dresses up anymore. Nobody even irons.

lines.speaker: Stuffed Shirt
lines.text: Hmph! Round two!

lines.speaker: Stuffed Shirt
lines.text: Round {n}. Still starched.

lines.speaker: Stuffed Shirt
lines.text: ...one doesn't RUN in a ballroom.

lines.speaker: Stuffed Shirt
lines.text: I was ironed in 1971. I've stayed ironed.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: A lady left this coat with me in 1971. She said she'd be right back.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: I have held on for fifty-five years. That's my whole job. Holding on.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: Hang on! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: Round {n}. Still holding on.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: ...ticket seven. I'm holding ticket seven.

lines.speaker: The Hanger-On
lines.text: She said she'd be right back. 1971.

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: Fifty-five years in this deck. Every game they play, they take me out first.

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: I'm wild. WILD. Nobody ever plays me.

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: Rematch! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: Round {n}. Best {n} out of {n}.

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: ...rigged. The whole game is RIGGED.

lines.speaker: The Sore Loser
lines.text: Best two out of three. Best three out of five.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: Every dance, I stood right here. Every song. Nobody ever asked.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: I'm not shy. I'm just very, very good at walls.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: Oh no. Round two.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: Round {n}. Still against the wall.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: ...I'm fine here. By the wall. With the wall.

lines.speaker: The Wallflower
lines.text: Nobody asked me. In 1971. Or since.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: Every full moon they danced under me. Then the last dance, and the doors closed.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: If I'm the brightest thing in the sky, somebody will HAVE to come.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: From the top! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: Round {n}. The band plays on.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: ...one more song. Just one.

lines.speaker: The Mirrorball
lines.text: They said see you next moon. 1971.

lines.speaker: Carry-On
lines.text: I've been packed since 1989. Nobody ever came to pick me up.

lines.speaker: Carry-On
lines.text: Everybody says I'm too big. I'm just very prepared.

lines.speaker: Carry-On
lines.text: Wheels up! Round two!

lines.speaker: Carry-On
lines.text: Round {n}. Still fits. Probably.

lines.speaker: Carry-On
lines.text: ...it fits. It FITS. Push harder.

lines.speaker: Carry-On
lines.text: Twenty-two inches. I'm exactly twenty-two inches.

lines.speaker: Jet Lag
lines.text: Every clock in here says midnight. I've been tired since 1989.

lines.speaker: Jet Lag
lines.text: I flew in from somewhere. I forget where. It was later there.

lines.speaker: Jet Lag
lines.text: Yawn. Round two.

lines.speaker: Jet Lag
lines.text: Round {n}. Still not sure what time it is.

lines.speaker: Jet Lag
lines.text: ...what time is it. What DAY is it.

lines.speaker: Jet Lag
lines.text: Five more minutes. Five more hours.

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: Nobody has reached the front of me since 1989. That's what a line is FOR.

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: I'm very long. I'm very, very good at being long.

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: Back of the line! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: Round {n}. Still waiting.

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: ...please wait. Please wait. Please wait.

lines.speaker: The Long Line
lines.text: Next. No. Not you. Wait.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: I've gone round this carousel since 1989. Every bag got picked up. Not me.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: I have sixty stickers. I've been everywhere. Nobody came to get me.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: Round and round! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: Round {n}. Round and round.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: ...round and round. Round and round.

lines.speaker: The Unclaimed
lines.text: Somebody will come. Somebody always comes.

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: I got here first. In 1989. I've been saving these seats ever since.

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: Sharing is for people with window seats.

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: Hey! I was sitting there! Round two!

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: Round {n}. Still mine.

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: ...mine. Both of them. Mine.

lines.speaker: The Armrest Hog
lines.text: The middle seat gets nothing. That's the RULE.

lines.speaker: The Last Call
lines.text: Flight Zero was due out at midnight. 1989. Nobody came to the gate.

lines.speaker: The Last Call
lines.text: I've called it every night since. Somebody has to answer.

lines.speaker: The Last Call
lines.text: DING. Round two. Please have your pass ready.

lines.speaker: The Last Call
lines.text: Round {n}. Still boarding.

lines.speaker: The Last Call
lines.text: ...Flight Zero. Now boarding. Now boarding.

lines.speaker: The Last Call
lines.text: Midnight. It's always midnight. That way nobody is late.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: I have never once got to fly. I only call it.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: Paused is safe. Nobody is late. Nobody is lost.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: DING. Final call. Please have your pass ready.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: Round {n}. Still boarding.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: ...now boarding. Now boarding. Please. Somebody.

lines.speaker: FINAL CALL
lines.text: Every other town is happy. That is the whole job.

lines.speaker: Lost Luggage
lines.text: Nobody has asked for me in a very long time. I stopped asking, too.

lines.speaker: Lost Luggage
lines.text: I have a sock. It isn’t mine. I’m keeping it anyway.

lines.speaker: Lost Luggage
lines.text: Back on the belt! Round two!

lines.speaker: Lost Luggage
lines.text: Round {n}. Still unclaimed.

lines.speaker: Lost Luggage
lines.text: ...it’s mine. It’s probably mine. Is it mine?

lines.speaker: Lost Luggage
lines.text: Please. Check the tag. Somebody must have the other half.

lines.speaker: Red-Eye
lines.text: I left at midnight and landed at midnight. I don’t know where the time went.

lines.speaker: Red-Eye
lines.text: Everyone gets off. I just keep going.

lines.speaker: Red-Eye
lines.text: Yaaawn. Round two.

lines.speaker: Red-Eye
lines.text: Round {n}. Still not sure what time it is.

lines.speaker: Red-Eye
lines.text: ...five more minutes. Five more years.

lines.speaker: Red-Eye
lines.text: Is it morning? It’s still tonight. It’s always tonight.

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: I got a seat once. Then somebody bigger got it.

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: Everyone else gets on. I just keep track of who doesn’t.

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: Back of the list! Round two!

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: Round {n}. Still on standby.

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: ...seventeen. It’s seventeen. They’ll call seventeen.

lines.speaker: Standby Sprite
lines.text: Please remain seated until your number is called.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: I have been red for a very long time.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: Everybody else got to go. I am the one who holds them.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: HONK. Lane closure. Round two.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: Round {n}. Still red.

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: ...Green. That was green. Was that green?

lines.speaker: Gridlock Prime
lines.text: Somebody go first. I’ll follow. I’m always last.

lines.speaker: Dual-Coast Drill Worm
lines.text: I have been digging since 1952. Nobody told me when to stop.

lines.speaker: Dual-Coast Drill Worm
lines.text: They called me a worm. I was a union drill.

lines.text: Bready Mercury is safe, the squirrels signed a treaty, and I owe the landlord a fence.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Go. I'll feed the starter. Twice a day, room temperature, no squirrels. I wrote it down.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara spots a squirrel across the street. She looks at the squirrel. She looks at Tom.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: She picks Tom. She leans on his legs for one long minute.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Then she picks the squirrel. Fair enough.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Somewhere down there, a squirrel is plotting.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Not my problem. For six whole hours.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Los Angeles again? I'm starting to think you live there.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The girls stay home. School tomorrow. Library books are due.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, I checked out a book about Los Angeles. Now I'll know where you are. Every minute.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I checked out a book about a pig. It's not about Los Angeles. It's better.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Both excellent choices. Return them on time.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That library has had enough excitement for one year.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Six hours of quiet. The library would be proud.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...I already miss Rose shushing everybody at full volume.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Airport. No eating in my cab. I can smell the potluck on you. It smells amazing. Still no.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Forty loaves, zero leftovers. Not bad for two guys and one oven.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Go open your fancy letter. Wear the blue shirt. I fixed the button. You're welcome.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara is still full from the potluck. She lifts one paw. That's all she can manage.

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Tom shakes it. "Deal. Back soon."

lines.speaker: Nara
lines.text: Nara lets out one very satisfied burp. Then she waddles home.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A letter with a seal. Nobody sends a seal for good news.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Or do they? Six hours to think about it. Great.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Downtown LA. Seventy-two and sunny. I didn't have to check.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Six hours, no fish, and a pepper to find for Boppy. In that order.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Long Island. Quiet. Thursday is conference night. It won't stay quiet.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! You're BACK! That's TWO times!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Mom made you a binder. It has TABS.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Did you bring the snacks? Tata. The SNACKS.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB packed them. Check my bag. Carefully. He also packed a note.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm checking NOW.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Downtown LA. Five hours and fifty-one minutes. Amy will want the number.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...Is that a squirrel on the cab? That's a squirrel on the cab.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Long Island. Quiet. Library quiet. That's a different kind.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! THREE times! The library's still whispering. I SAID so. In a text.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It said my name. It said ROSE. Then it said shhh.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we go find out what it wants. After a sandwich.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm bringing a flashlight. And a pencil. For notes.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Downtown LA. It smells like somebody's grill. Everybody's grill.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: TNB says bring an empty stomach and forty bread pans. I've got the stomach.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Long Island. No moon tonight. Somebody's going to make that my problem.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! FOUR! I have a chart now. You're on it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Deedee has your letter. She hasn't opened it. She's LOOKED at it. A lot.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A wax seal with a clock on it. I'd look at it a lot too.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I named the seal Flippers.
